obernants.domain: Finite materialized directed adjacency lists of (usize,u8), a usize source, and Result<Vec<Option<usize>>,Error> observations. Allocation succeeds; immutable inputs. Binary valid graphs allow loops, parallel edges and cycles.
obernants.operator: In universe U of declared input/output pairs, the complement U\\graph(F) contains accepted invalid rows, wrong first errors, finite labels for unreachable vertices, nonminimal reachable labels, nonzero source labels, and length-mismatched vectors. This defines semantic nonbehavior, not merely the negative test list.
obernants.assumptions: Successful allocations; mathematical path semantics; finite oracle correspondence only.
obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation with finite evidence, no formal semantic proof.

obernants.domain: Finite materialized directed adjacency lists of (usize,u8), a usize source, and Result<Vec<Option<usize>>,Error> observations. Allocation succeeds; immutable inputs. Binary valid graphs allow loops, parallel edges and cycles.
obernants.operator: For an Ok vector d of length n, compatible inputs are all valid binary G and s<n whose reachability equals the Some support and whose shortest-path lengths equal d. A sufficient and necessary certificate is d[s]=0, no edge from finite to None, d[v]<=d[u]+w on every finite-source edge, and for each finite v a witnessed s-to-v path of sum d[v]. Tight edges alone are insufficient because disconnected zero cycles could receive fake finite labels. Invalid-error preimages are inputs whose first failing check has exactly the reported payload. Recovery is generally many-to-one.
obernants.assumptions: Successful allocations; mathematical path semantics; finite oracle correspondence only.
obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation with finite evidence, no formal semantic proof.

obernants.operator: Adding an edge (u,v,w) with finite D[u], finite D[v] and D[v]<=D[u]+w preserves all shortest distances: substitute the old distance inequality through any new-edge path. A duplicate edge always preserves distances. An edge from an unreachable vertex also preserves distances unless some other edit makes that vertex reachable.
